claim_boundary.allowed_claim: The current governance, research, and prototype groups have a path-backed inventory, resolvable test selectors, observed dependency checks, hash-bound exit evidence, and a non-destructive removal-impact dry run.
claim_boundary.forbidden_claim: This one registry and one verification run do not prove longitudinal maintenance cost, migration feasibility in operation, or ECO-03 closure.

components.owner: Javen retains final authority; AI agents maintain candidate governance artifacts.
components.purpose: Define and verify the local paper workbench's scope, authority, evidence, acceptance, and project-method controls.

responsibility.summary: Own normative controls and deterministic governance verification for the project.

contract_interface.summary: Machine-readable candidate contract and project-method policy consumed by governance verification.

dependencies.reason: Governance binds research artifacts and research sufficiency into its candidate boundary.
Governance protects and references the existing paper-only prototype boundary.

failure_mode.summary: Self-consistent governance labels can report closure without executable or independently bound evidence.
failure_mode.detection: Strict JSON, evidence hashes, selector resolution, observed dependency edges, layer checks, and review freshness fail closed.
failure_mode.containment: Keep status partial and prevent the registry from asserting longitudinal cost proof or ECO-03 closure.

preconditions: A replacement authority and acceptance boundary is registered.
Every research and prototype reference is migrated and reverified.
The governance test selector is removed or reassigned with review evidence.
steps: Run the removal-impact dry run and preserve its blocker report.
Migrate each observed dependency and rerun the declared governance selector.
Obtain a fresh review binding before removing the governance scope root.
Freeze the final accepted governance state and enumerate all consumers.
Move authority and verification responsibilities to an explicitly reviewed successor before retirement.
Recompute dependency edges and require zero remaining cross-component references.
rollback_steps: Rerun governance verification and its declared test selector.

components.owner: Javen owns research decisions; AI agents maintain bounded candidate evidence and preregistrations.
components.purpose: Preserve preregistered research questions, frozen evidence, counterevidence, and bounded-incomplete decision records.

responsibility.summary: Own bounded research artifacts and their evidence-preservation boundary.

contract_interface.summary: Finite or explicitly bounded research inputs whose status and stopping rules remain visible.

failure_mode.summary: Mutable or incomplete evidence can be relabelled as sufficient, exhaustive, or decision-closing.
failure_mode.detection: Hash-bound preregistration anchors and a resolvable research-sufficiency selector expose missing or stale evidence.
failure_mode.containment: Preserve bounded-incomplete states and forbid open-web exhaustiveness claims.

preconditions: Governance no longer references research paths.
Decision-relevant source bytes and hashes are archived under a registered successor.
The research-sufficiency selector is removed or reassigned.
steps: Run the removal-impact dry run and enumerate governance dependents.
Migrate decision-relevant evidence with hashes and status history intact.
Recompute dependency edges and require no governance-to-research edge.
Preserve exact source bytes, hashes, preregistration order, and bounded findings.
Update every governance locator before changing the research root.
Rerun the declared selector and obtain a fresh review.
rollback_steps: Restore the archived research tree at its original relative paths.
Recompute hashes and rerun the research-sufficiency selector.
